subject.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally execute standalone JSON assistant content as a shared compatibility fallback, or should the linked failure be repaired only in native Ollama tool-call conversion?
rationale: The patch changes shared text-to-execution semantics, while the canonical report expects native structured calls and the current proof cannot distinguish the two paths.

options.title: Prove strict fallback and native path
options.body: Require valid end-to-end evidence, align classifiers, and retain only JSON shapes observed in real provider output.

options.title: Repair native conversion only
options.body: If the raw response already contains structured tool_calls, fix Ollama conversion and omit the shared fallback expansion.

options.title: Pause pending evidence
options.body: Keep the draft open until the real response shape settles the ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Prove strict fallback and native path
recommendation.body: Require valid end-to-end evidence, align classifiers, and retain only JSON shapes observed in real provider output.

likelyOwner.reason: The Ollama stream and shared provider compatibility history most strongly route this cross-provider execution-boundary decision to steipete.
